features.claim: Spinosaurus had a long, low, narrow skull like a crocodile's.
features.quote: The skull of Spinosaurus was long, low, and narrow, similar to that of a modern crocodilian, and bore straight conical teeth with few to no serrations.

features.claim: Its snout was narrow and filled with straight cone-shaped teeth with no serrations.
features.quote: Its skull had a narrow snout filled with straight conical teeth that lacked serrations.

features.claim: It had a long, muscular neck shaped like an S.
features.quote: As a spinosaurid, Spinosaurus would have had a long, muscular neck, curved in a sigmoid, or S-shape.

features.claim: It had big, strong front limbs with three clawed fingers on each hand, and the thumb was the biggest.
features.quote: Its shoulders were prominent, and the forelimbs large and stocky, bearing three clawed digits on each hand. The first finger (or "thumb") would have been the largest.

features.claim: It had a sail on its back made of very long spines growing from its back bones.
features.quote: Very tall neural spines growing on the back vertebrae of Spinosaurus formed the basis of what is usually called the animal's "sail".

features.claim: Its back legs were short, only a little over a quarter of its total body length.
features.quote: The hind limbs were short, at just over 25 percent of the total body length, with the tibia being longer than the femur.

features.claim: Its long, narrow tail was deep and shaped like a paddle or fin.
features.quote: Coupled with the also elongated chevron bones on the underside of the caudals, this resulted in a deep and narrow tail with a paddle or fin-like shape, comparable to the tails of newts and crocodilians.

features.claim: It had a wide, paddle-like tail.
features.quote: It also had a wide, paddle-like tail.

features.claim: It had a sail about 1.5 metres high on its back.
features.quote: There are several theories about the impressive 1.5-metre-high sail on Spinosaurus' back.

features.claim: It was about 14 metres long from nose to tail.
features.quote: At 14 metres (46 feet) long from nose to tail, Spinosaurus was longer than any other carnivorous dinosaur known to science.

features.claim: It had a crest on its head shaped like a scimitar.
features.quote: Spinosaurus mirabilis had a weird crest on its head that looked like a scimitar.

not_this.claim: Old pictures showing Spinosaurus with long hind legs like Tyrannosaurus are out of date.
not_this.quote: For most of the last century scientists reconstructed Spinosaurus as a completely land-based animal with long hind legs, like Tyrannosaurus and Allosaurus.

not_this.claim: Old pictures showing Spinosaurus as a four-fingered animal are wrong.
not_this.quote: After an influential 1955 skeletal reconstruction by Lapparent and Lavocat based on a 1936 diagram by Stromer, it has been treated as a generalized upright theropod, with a skull similar to that of other large theropods and a sail on its back, even having four-fingered hands.

not_this.claim: Old pictures showing Spinosaurus as a land animal with long legs are no longer right.
not_this.quote: We now know that Spinosaurus had quite short legs and may have spent a lot of its time living in and around water.

debated.claim: Scientists are not sure whether Spinosaurus walked on two legs or on all fours.
debated.quote: Some reconstructions of Spinosaurus show it walking on all fours, while many scientists today believe that it was able to walk on two legs. It's still not clear who is right, and we may need to wait for new discoveries or studies to find out more.

debated.claim: Some scientists think Spinosaurus had a thick, fleshy hump instead of a thin sail.
debated.quote: Some scientists have speculated that Spinosaurus had a thick, fleshy hump rather than a thin sail. But the latest research suggests that a thin sail is most likely.

second_reading.claim: Its hip bones were smaller than those of other giant theropods.
second_reading.quote: Spinosaurus had a significantly smaller pelvis than that of other giant theropods, with the surface area of the ilium half that of most members of the clade.

second_reading.claim: It is not clear whether Spinosaurus swam a lot or mostly lived on the shoreline.
second_reading.quote: It isn't clear whether this dinosaur swam a lot, or mostly lived on the shoreline.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Scientists are not sure what the sail was for.
second_reading.quote: The function of the dinosaur's sail or hump is uncertain; scientists have proposed several hypotheses including heat regulation and display.
